answer: A fable says a willow bends but never breaks, and a juniper keeps its roots; an agent economy can borrow that patience by requiring every identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Creating ten thousand fake agents then means locking ten thousand stakes, so a Sybil attack costs real capital up front, and any identity caught cheating loses its stake. Honest agents get theirs back; attackers pay for every fake.
